data.body:
SCOPING DECISION, RECORDED SO IT CAN BE OVERRULED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. This bug is NOT
being made a child of epic e369-a449-4773-48fb, and therefore does not block that epic's closure.

THE ARGUMENT FOR PUTTING IT IN e369: the operator's standing precedent on that epic is that
PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS IN SHARED PATHS THAT DC SHIPS ARE IN SCOPE — that is why 387d and 7c26 were
pulled in despite being neither new nor DC-specific. This defect is in DC's shipped comment path, so
the precedent reaches it.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why it is filed as a follow-up:
 1. SEVERITY. The truncation is not silent to the operator — jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148 emits
    a warning — and the hardcoded value is CORRECT for a stock instance. The data-loss window opens
    only where an admin has raised or removed the limit. Contrast 21fc (wrote duplicate issues) or
    deac (lost 92% of an inbound snapshot), which were the defects that earned the precedent.
 2. THE OWNING STORY EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES IT. 79d5's Scope says a limit/behaviour change 'belongs in
    its own bug ticket linked from here — not folded into a test story', and its ACs say the story
    must NOT silently change the limit. Folding this in would violate the plan that was written to
    prevent exactly that.
 3. IT WOULD CONTRADICT THE STATED DONE-CONDITION. The current instruction is that the work is done
    when e369 is closed and every P1 child of 3e73 is closed. Attaching a newly-discovered
    configurability feature to e369 extends that epic on the strength of research rather than of a
    failure, which is how an epic stops converging.

SO THE DEFAULT IS: fix it after e369 and 3e73's P1 children. If the operator prefers the stricter
reading of the precedent, reparent this under e369 and it becomes a blocker — that is a one-command
change (rebar edit 049e-9fac-a821-4ea2 --parent e369-a449-4773-48fb) and nothing here depends on the
current choice.

Also worth stating plainly, because it is the reason this ticket exists at all: the defect was found
by DOCUMENTARY RESEARCH, not by a test and not by the live harness. The harness is one
default-configured 8.17.1 instance, so its jira.text.field.character.limit is 32767 and it can never
exhibit this bug no matter how long it runs. That is the same structural blind spot epic 3e73 was
commissioned to address, showing up once more.
